newsitem.title: CHINA: China punishes papers for "reporting mistakes".
newsitem.headline: China punishes papers for "reporting mistakes".

text.p: China's securities authorities have suspended the right of two key newspapers to release official information about listed companies because of "mistakes in reporting", the China Securities newspaper said on Saturday.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), the top securities watchdog, withdrew the right of the Shanghai Securities News and the Shenzhen-based Securities Times to release such information from Dec 1 to 31, the newspaper said.
The information covered includes official company statements, prospectuses for stock issues, annual reports and the decisions of shareholders' meetings.
Only newspapers designated by the CSRC can publish such information. The other two newspapers with the right to publish company releases are the China Securities News and the Financial News.

An official at the CSRC said she had no information about the decision and that the officials involved would only be available on Monday. Officials of the two newspapers were not available for comment.
Shanghai brokers said the "mistakes" could possibly have been comments about stocks published in the two newspapers that contradicted official policy in some way.
Earlier this month, the CSRC issued an urgent circular ordering designated newspapers to report more fully about the risks of stock investment.
